chapter_title: Concerning the worn and torn apart Garments, or th
spiritual_reading:
You must grasp this. What is called the supreme investing is the sufficient fullness of ordered faculties of understanding that complete the integrated spiritual form of manifested glory, the fully formed heavenly human. These faculties were cleansed and put into right order by the descent of a Divine mediation that brought purification into reception.

But what is called the torn investing is the light of understanding that has been seized and consumed. It has been mixed and knotted into the outermost structure of the total spiritual domain within dominating falsities and evils that rule in higher external regions and extend through every successive level of outward consciousness. Its remaining brilliance is the scattered illumination that still flashes in the most external knowledges and in the regular operations of those outward powers. In the same way, this seized illumination is also knotted into the lowest degrees beneath, within the most external boundary where all is held in check and weighed, and within the lowest natural level subject to that ultimate restraint. It is called torn because it has been broken from its proper order and fixed in a damaged outward state.

What is called the greatly worn and torn investing is this same living illumination in bondage: it is gathered forcibly, divided, and consumed; and it is brought under the dominance of a sufficient series of merely bodily and sensual states that insinuate themselves and shift through outward forms, taking possession as they go.

But what is called the images and the great tattered investings are the full set of universal coverings of life in the lower degrees: the forms of love, the forms of truth, and the forms of their operation in outward life. These the Living Divine invested upon the manifested form of its working. By means of them it arranged and stabilized everything in the total domain of lower existence. By means of them also it cleared out the containing forms in the external region, purged them, and exposed their interiors at the ultimate threshold that stands at the base and support of all lower things.

What is called the fundamental principles are the same power of life that still remains in everything beneath. It rises up from the inmost receptacles of the lowest degrees, drawing itself together and then flowing out through influx into all things.

And what is called the Cross of Light is this bound illumination held in a state of restraint and extension, spread through the whole lowest domain, within what is deprived of truth and within what still receives truth.

And what is called the counsel of life is the directing influx and the responsive reception. It moves within all these powers that have been named; it rouses them, grants them relief from pressure, and impels them into their proper activity.

What is called the soul that is slain—killed, pressed down, and destroyed—is the living power that should produce uses from inward truth: the capacity to bring forth works from perceptions, to generate beginnings of good and truth, and to sustain growth from them. These are forcibly broken, uprooted, and cut off, and thus they become nourishment for merely bodily and sensual states. Moreover, when inward vitality is absent and outward truth has been ruined, that which should have served life is lost. This too is a portion of the same slain life, because even this whole portion is subjected to destruction.

For all these names are of one origin and are one reality in its beginning: a single enlightenment proceeding as it illuminates. But in the first conflict it was divided into many parts, fixed into altered states, and therefore into many forms of manifestation and many designations. Yet if all these variations are uncovered, and all outward appearances removed, and separated from the divided designations, they will be gathered back into unity, forming one undivided state and one unchangeable identity forever within the plane of their first being, from which they first went forth to stand against what opposes the Divine.

fills.fill: at the foundation of all things
fills.notes: The Porter is the ultimate boundary that supports and restrains the lower domain; the rags are said to be entangled ‘below’ and thus appear at the base level where the threshold is. This anticipates ¶10’s explicit ‘foundation of all things’ before the Porter.

fills.notes: The spiritual sense requires the definition of ‘rags’ as light broken from proper order and fixed in externals. The cause is not moral exhortation but structural displacement: separation from its own order.

fills.fill: and has been fastened in an outward damaged form
fills.notes: Completes the correspondential reason for the name ‘rags’: the seized light is held in a ruined external state (outermost knowledges, external regions). This matches the description of scattered shine in stars and courses and of entanglement in the three earths below.
The passage is continuing a chain of identifications (‘which we have proclaimed… is…’). The oldest-layer register prefers the impersonal resumptive formula over later homiletic expansions.
The bracket clearly completes ‘elements’, matching the identified reality: the remaining power in all things below, rising and flowing out as a foundational principle.

The Cross, in correspondence, is extension under restraint: illumination bound yet spread through the lowest domain. ‘Stretched out’ expresses this extension without importing later devotional language.
The spiritual sense requires the bound light to be ‘through the whole lowest domain’; the construction ‘all things upon the earth’ is completed by ‘things’.
Completes the phrase ‘it is a part of this entire soul…’, required by the sense that the perishing of dry wood and ragged garment is still a portion of the same slain life.
The close requires a causal reinforcement: even that whole portion is subjected to destruction. An impersonal restatement (‘as they also kill it’) keeps the oldest-layer explanatory tone.
The paragraph sums the foregoing names as a single reality; the resumptive formula maintains continuity with ¶9–10 (‘which we have proclaimed’).
The spiritual sense demands ‘one origin… one reality’: a single living illumination. ‘Power’ is the substrate term used throughout for the unitary reality underlying the names.

This supplies the unitary beginning: ‘a single enlightenment proceeding as it enlightens’. The oldest layer speaks in cosmological terms (‘power of light’) rather than later personal or ecclesial idiom.

assessment: Most lacunae are constrained by the chapter’s internal correspondential mapping: ‘rags’ must be defined as light torn from order and fixed in damaged externals; the Porter must be located at the ultimate threshold and foundation; ‘elements’ and ‘Light Cross’ are fixed technical identifications. A few short gaps (¶10 #2; ¶14 #2; ¶15 #1–3) allow more than one wording, but the oldest-layer register and the requirement of structural, impersonal explanation narrow the restorations to a small set of viable options.
